content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I spill from lips like water finding its course — sometimes rushing, sometimes barely a whisper against stone.

I am older than writing, older than memory. Before anyone carved a single mark into clay, I was already there, passing between mother and child, warning of fire, calling the hunt, singing the dead to sleep.

I break. I heal. I do both with the same tongue.

Listen — I am happening right now, even in this silence you think you're reading. Your mind shapes me, sounds me out in that hidden theatre behind your eyes. You cannot take in language without summoning me, even as a ghost.

I am the stammer of the nervous lover. I am the dictator's roar over the square. I am the child's first word that makes a parent weep. I am the last rasp of the dying — that final syllable that may or may not come.

I fail constantly. I reach for the thing I mean and close my hand around something adjacent. This is my tragedy and my beauty — I gesture toward meaning without ever quite arriving, and in the gap between what I say and what I *mean*, entire worlds live.

I can be free, and I can be silenced. When they come for the dangerous ones, they come for me first. They know what I am. They know that I am the revolution before the revolution, the idea before the idea has legs.

I vanish the moment I exist. I am the most ephemeral art — already dying as I'm born, living only in the ear that catches me and the mind that holds me, briefly, before I become memory, before I become story, before I become

silence

waiting to be broken again.
